_doc: Concept-first briefs (Nick, 2026-09-04 afternoon). `concept` is the agreed creature paragraph in animal language. `readings` are distinct short briefs derived from it, each a different visual reading; a divergent sheet runs every reading on every model with a few seeds and Nick picks a direction. `banned` words never appear in a prompt: klein renders machine nouns as hardware.

frackworm.concept: The Frackworm is a living auger. Its head is not a tool fixed to a worm but the worm's own skull, grown into a blunt spiral horn of armor, ridged like a cone snail's shell, the ridges worn smooth by rock. Behind the horn the armor breaks into heavy overlapping bands like an armadillo's, each as thick as the segment it covers, and the body under them is as wide as the head: a twelve-meter, three-tonne mass that looks heavier than anything near it. Its eyes are two small dark beads set deep in the first band behind the horn, the eyes of an animal that lives in the dark and does not need to see far. Its signature is the burst: when it sets the horn against rock, slurry blasts out from the seams between the head bands in a violent pressure fan of wet sand and rock chips, the way a whale blows, not the way a hose pours. Its stance is planted and patient, a working juggernaut rather than a monster, the kind of creature a crew would trust beside them.

readings.A: A giant armored worm seen from the side, planted low and heavy. Its head is its own skull grown into a blunt spiral horn like a cone snail's shell, ridges worn smooth. Behind the horn, thick overlapping armor bands like an armadillo's run the whole body, which is as wide as the head and coiled with weight. Two small bead eyes sit deep in the first band. From the seams between the head bands a violent fan of wet sand and rock chips bursts outward, like a whale blowing.
readings.B: A giant armored worm in three-quarter view, its blunt spiral horn of a head turned toward the viewer. The horn is the animal's own skull, ridged like a cone snail's shell. Heavy overlapping armor bands like an armadillo's cover a body as wide as the head, a massive weight curling back behind it. Two small bead eyes are set deep in the first band behind the horn. A hard pressure fan of wet sand and rock chips bursts from the seams of the head bands to both sides.
readings.C: A giant armored worm rearing up at a diagonal, its blunt spiral horn head at the top, ridged like a cone snail's shell and worn smooth. Thick overlapping armor bands like an armadillo's cover a body as wide as the head, its lower coils resting heavy on the ground line of the figure. Two small bead eyes sit deep in the first band. Wet sand and rock chips burst in a violent fan from the seams between the head bands. A patient working giant, not a monster.
readings.A2: A giant armored worm seen from the side, planted low and heavy. Its head is a broad blunt cone, as wide at its base as the body and grown of the same armor, ringed by worn spiral ridges that wind to a rounded point; the head is the animal's own skull, not anything attached to it, and it has no snout, no jaw line and no neck. Behind the head, thick overlapping armor bands like an armadillo's run the whole body, which is as wide as the head everywhere and coiled with weight. Two small bead eyes sit deep in the first band behind the head. From the seams between the head bands a violent fan of wet sand and rock chips bursts outward, like a whale blowing.
readings.C2: A giant armored worm with its front third lifted off the ground at a diagonal, the rest of the body resting in heavy coils; it is a worm as thick as its head from end to end, never a snake. Thick overlapping armor bands like an armadillo's cover the whole body. Two small bead eyes sit deep in the first band behind the head. Wet sand and rock chips burst in a violent fan from the seams between the head bands. A patient working giant, not a monster.

readings.H3: A giant armored worm seen from the side, planted low and heavy. Its whole head is a boring cone like the front of a giant earthworm hardened into a tapered spiral shell, the kind of shell a turret snail wears, as wide at its base as the body and winding in smooth worn ridges to a rounded point. It is the animal's own skull, not anything attached. Behind the head, thick overlapping armor bands like an armadillo's run the whole body, which is as wide as the head everywhere and coiled with weight. Two small bead eyes sit deep in the first band behind the head. From the seams between the head bands a violent fan of wet sand and rock chips bursts outward, like a whale blowing.
readings.A3: A giant armored worm seen from the side, planted low with its weight down, its body as thick as a tree trunk from head to tail. Its head is a blunt tapering cone of the same armor, pointing straight ahead along the line of the body, level with the ground, not tilted up. Thick overlapping armor bands like an armadillo's cover the whole body. Two small bead eyes sit deep in the first band behind the head. The most violent thing in the picture is the burst: from the seams between the head bands a huge fan of wet sand and rock chips blasts forward and outward, the fan as wide as the head, drawn as heavy solid streams and flying chunks, like a whale blowing.
